title: How a privileged token function drained the 79AU pool
dek: Nine token pulls. Three recipients. A permission that remained more powerful than the pool’s liquidity protections.
asOf: October 9, 2026 report snapshot · all times UTC
author: ChainBounty Research

blocks.title: The permission behind the drain
paragraphs: On October 7, a privileged token function moved 79AU out of a PancakeSwap pool without payment. Recipients could sell tokens back for USDT. Burned LP receipts did not remove this token-level authority.
This interactive reading edition summarizes the published ChainBounty article. Figures retain its October 9 snapshot; they are not live balances or independently verified findings.

blocks.title: The authority remained the issue
paragraphs: The published account records no recovery at its October 9 snapshot. It leaves key theft versus insider misuse unresolved; destination-chain payouts remain outside its scope.
takeaways: Follow the identified holdings and custodial lead.
Revoke residual pull permissions or migrate the contract.
A negotiation is not evidence of returned assets.
